name: Car wash and detailing

problems.words: A car gets scratched and the customer says we did it
quick_ideas: Photograph every car before work starts, so its condition is on record
Point out existing marks to the customer at drop-off, so it's agreed upfront.

workzap_build.text: before-and-after photos per car saved against each job with time stamp, at every site and van.

problems.ask_first: Does this happen mostly with new customers, or with regulars, and is it usually a scratch that was already there?
problems.free_stops: The photo routine and storage are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many cars leave with pre-work condition notes this week against total cars detailed, so dispute exposure on your own process is clearer.
Make one person own the walk-round note before keys are taken, so every car starts with the same visible condition record.

problems.words: Basement washers mark cars done that weren't washed
quick_ideas: Ask for a photo of each finished car instead of a tick, so there's proof of work
Spot-check a few cars each week, so the team knows proof matters.

workzap_build.text: a job list per washer with photo proof of each car, location and time, summarised for the owner each morning.

problems.ask_first: How does a washer show today that a car was done?
problems.free_stops: How the job list and proof are set up is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare marked done cars with a same-day walk round of actual finished cars, so false completion is measured on the job itself.
Give one supervisor the job of checking one written done list before any car is marked complete, so basement updates match washed cars.

problems.words: Subscription customers say they didn't get their washes
quick_ideas: Record each wash against the customer's package, so there's a count to share
Send customers their monthly count, with their permission, so questions are answered before complaints.

workzap_build.text: a subscription record of washes used, renewal date and payment status, with monthly summaries sent to the owner.

problems.ask_first: Do these customers say they missed washes at one branch or time, or is it spread across the whole month?
problems.free_stops: Package tracking and summary timing are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many subscription customers asked about missed washes this month, so you can see how often proof is failing before renewals.
Keep one running wash log for each package in one notebook, so any customer query can be answered from the same record.

problems.words: Monthly package payments come late or not at all
quick_ideas: List who has paid this month and who hasn't, so you know the gap
Remind late payers once, so it's raised early.

workzap_build.text: package payment tracking with payment reminders and receipts sent to customers.

problems.ask_first: Is it a few package customers who are always late, or many of them each month?
problems.free_stops: Reminder steps are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which monthly package customers are late at week end compared with who was due, so the collection backlog is visible early.
Give one person the job of updating one due list every afternoon, so unpaid packages are followed from a single place.

problems.words: Weekend queues are so long people drive away
quick_ideas: Count how many cars leave without being served on a busy day, so you see the size of it
Offer regular customers a booked slot, so walk-ins spread out.

workzap_build.text: WhatsApp booking with time slots per service and bay, confirmations and reminders.

problems.ask_first: Is it every weekend all day, or only a few peak hours on one day?
problems.free_stops: Slot rules per service are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many cars arrive, wait, and leave on the busiest shift, so you can see where queue loss is hurting weekends.
Give one person the job of keeping one waiting list at busy times, so arrivals are handled in order and fewer drivers give up.

problems.words: Bookings come on WhatsApp, Instagram and calls and get mixed up
quick_ideas: Put every booking into one diary, whatever the channel, so there's one list
Give one person the job of confirming bookings, so nothing is assumed.

workzap_build.text: one place where bookings from every channel land, with confirmations and reminders sent to customers.

problems.ask_first: Which channel causes most of the mix-ups, WhatsApp, Instagram or phone calls?
problems.free_stops: Channel set-up and confirmation flow are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare bookings received with cars that actually arrive over a few days, so missed or duplicated entries stop hiding inside mixed channels.
Give one staff member one paper booking list for every channel, so all incoming jobs land in the same daily queue.

problems.words: Shampoo, wax and cloth usage keeps going up
quick_ideas: Issue consumables from one store, so you know what goes out
Compare what was used against cars washed this week, so you get a first picture.

workzap_build.text: a consumables issue log with usage per car and alerts on unusual use.

problems.ask_first: Is it one item, like shampoo, that is rising fastest, or all of them together?
problems.free_stops: How usage is measured per service is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note cloth, shampoo and wax issued at opening and what remains at closing, so rising use is tied to the day's car count.
Give one person the job of handing out consumables from one shelf, so extra usage stops being spread across the whole site.

problems.words: Walk-in cash doesn't match the car count
quick_ideas: Give a numbered token or slip for every car, so cars can be counted
Count cash against slips at closing, so gaps show the same day.

workzap_build.text: a daily cash-up matched to cars washed per site.

problems.ask_first: Is the cash usually short on the same days or with the same staff, or does it vary?
problems.free_stops: The cash-up steps are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the walk-in car tally at closing with cash received the same day, so the size of the cash gap is no longer guessed.
Give one cashier one closing sheet for car count and cash together, so any mismatch is caught before the next shift starts.

problems.words: Each washer does it his own way
quick_ideas: Agree what "done" means for each service level, so everyone works to one standard
Show it to new washers on day one, so training is consistent.

workzap_build.text: service checklists on phone per wash level, ticked by the washer, with quality visible by site.

problems.ask_first: Is the difference mostly in how long each washer takes, or in how clean the car is at the end?
problems.free_stops: The checklists themselves are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Watch the same service done by different washers and note where their finish differs, so inconsistency is seen in the actual work.
Give one lead washer the job of checking every finished car against one written service list, so quality stops changing by person.

problems.words: Coating customers don't come back for maintenance
quick_ideas: Tell each coating customer when maintenance is due, so they leave with a date
Ask permission to remind them, so you can follow up.

workzap_build.text: maintenance reminders sent to ceramic and PPF customers when due.

problems.ask_first: Do coating customers simply forget maintenance, or do they go to another place for it?
problems.free_stops: Reminder timing is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note how many coated cars returned for maintenance this week against how many were originally delivered, so the missed follow-up load is clear.
Give one staff member the job of keeping one notebook page of coating handover dates, so maintenance calls happen when customers still expect them.

never_say: Advice on water discharge, chemical storage or environmental permits.
Who is liable for damage, or insurance advice.
Anything on workers' visas, housing, wages or hours; refer to a lawyer or labour adviser.
Covert tracking of workers; field proof is about the job, not the person.
Storing building access codes, parking details or addresses.
Typical pricing for coatings or packages.

sample_reply.person: We do basement washes across several buildings in Dubai. Customers say their car wasn't washed and my guys say it was. What can I do?
sample_reply.pi:
Yes, this can be brought under control, and the first steps are simple.
First, ask for a photo of each finished car instead of a tick, so there's proof of work.
Second, spot-check a few cars yourself each week, so the team knows the proof matters.
Workzap's part would be: a job list per washer with photo, time and location for every car, and a morning summary to you.

Shall I get a solution document and quote prepared for you? You're free to say no.
